e.etymology: A spelling of Marley, an English surname from places whose Old English names end in leah, a woodland clearing.

assoc.t: sounds like Marley, as in reggae legend Bob Marley

e.etymology: A modern respelling of Jackson, an English surname meaning son of Jack, with the nickname Jax written into it.
The Hebrew form of Judah, traditionally explained as praised. Judah was the fourth son of Jacob and Leah and founder of the tribe that gave the Jewish people their name.
The French form of Amelia, from Germanic names beginning with amal, vigor or work. The 2001 French film Amélie brought it to American attention.
namesakes: Amélie Poulain (heroine of the 2001 French film Amélie)

assoc.t: Amélie, the 2001 French romantic comedy film

e.etymology: From the Old French name Hughe, brought to England by the Normans, a short form of Germanic names beginning with hug, heart or mind.
A modern American coinage rhyming with Leilani. It can be read in Hawaiian as Mei, May, plus lani, heaven. Jersey Shore's Jenni Farley gave it to her daughter in 2014.
A respelling of Crew, the English word for a team and a surname from the town of Crewe in Cheshire. The spelling echoes the rock band Motley Crue.

assoc.t: Motley Crue, the 1980s heavy metal band

e.etymology: From Latin Livia, the feminine of Livius, a Roman family name possibly related to lividus, bluish. Livia Drusilla, wife of Augustus, was the most powerful woman of early imperial Rome.
namesakes: Livia Soprano (Tony's mother in The Sopranos)
Livia Drusilla (wife of the Roman emperor Augustus)

e.etymology: A spelling of Elise, the French short form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, God is my oath. The y invites a link with Elysium, which is folk etymology.
A one-n spelling of Gianna, the Italian short form of Giovanna, the feminine of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious.
An American coinage: a phonetic spelling of the initials J.C., or an elaboration of Jay and Jace, in the family of Jacey and Kaycee.
namesakes: Jaycee Dugard (kidnapping survivor and author of A Stolen Life)

assoc.t: the Jaycees, the US Junior Chamber civic organization

e.etymology: An anglicized form of Irish Aisling, dream or vision, reshaped with the -lyn ending; in the US it is also felt as a blend of Ashley and Lynn.
A modern American coinage built on the Jan- sound with the popular -iyah ending, alongside Aniyah and Saniyah.

e.meaning: my God is Yahweh; as a girls' name also from Greek helios, sun
e.etymology: In Italian, Elia is the men's form of Elijah, Hebrew for my God is Yahweh, and also a women's name from Latin Helia, from Greek helios, sun. In the US it is mostly given to girls.
namesakes: Elia Kazan (director of On the Waterfront)

e.etymology: From Arabic aliya, the feminine of ali, high or exalted. Hebrew aliyah, ascent, the word for moving to Israel, is a separate source of the same sound.

assoc.t: sounds like Aaliyah, the late R&B singer
aliyah, the Hebrew term for Jewish immigration to Israel

e.etymology: A respelling of Landon, an English surname from a place name, a variant of Langdon, long hill.

e.meaning: from Anahita, Persian goddess of the waters
e.etymology: A French name traced to Greek Anaitis, from Anahita, the Old Persian goddess of the waters; it is also taken as a Provençal form of Anna. The writer Anaïs Nin made it known.
e.note: Americans often misread it as uh-NAY or uh-NICE; the French pronunciation sounds the final s.

e.etymology: A name with several sources: Zaria is a city in northern Nigeria, zarya is a Slavic word for dawn, and in the US the name also works as an elaboration of Zara.

assoc.t: Zaria, a city in northern Nigeria

e.etymology: A Latinate form of Rosaline and Rosalind, a Germanic name long reinterpreted through Latin rosa, rose; in Spanish and Portuguese it is felt as an elaboration of Rosa.

assoc.t: Rosalina, the cosmic princess of Nintendo's Mario games

e.etymology: From French Joëlle, the feminine of Joel, Hebrew for Yahweh is God.
A spelling of Dylan, a Welsh name built from dy, great, and llanw, tide; in Welsh legend Dylan is a child of the sea. Dilan is a common spelling in Latin America. A Kurdish name Dilan is unrelated.
A variant of Ileana, the Romanian form of Helen, from Greek Helene, often linked to a word for torch. It is used in Spanish; Bulgarian Iliyana is a separate feminine of Elijah.
A modern variant of Cason, an English surname altered from the Norfolk place name Cawston. It also reads as Case with the -en ending.

e.meaning: will provide (from Jehovah-jireh, the Lord will provide)
e.etymology: From Jehovah-jireh, the Lord will provide, the name Abraham gives the place where a ram takes Isaac's place in Genesis 22. The 2021 worship song Jireh spread it as a given name.

assoc.t: Jireh, 2021 worship song by Elevation Worship

e.etymology: A pet form of Rudolph, from Germanic hrod, fame, and wulf, wolf; long used as a full name.
namesakes: Rudy Giuliani (former New York City mayor)
Rudy Ruettiger (Notre Dame walk-on of the film Rudy)

assoc.t: Rudy, the 1993 Notre Dame football film
Rudy Giuliani, former New York mayor

e.etymology: A spelling of Michaela, the feminine of Michael, from Hebrew Mikha'el, who is like God. Mikaela is the standard form in Sweden and Finland.
From a northern English and Scottish surname, Wat plus -son; Wat was the medieval short form of Walter.

assoc.t: IBM Watson, the AI system that won Jeopardy!

e.etymology: A shortened form of Dakarai, a Shona name from Zimbabwe meaning rejoice. In the US it has grown since the 2010s.
A traditional English short form of Christopher, and of Katherine by way of Kitty. It is now given on its own to boys and girls in nearly equal numbers.
namesakes: Kit Harington (Jon Snow in Game of Thrones)

assoc.t: kit, a set of parts or tools; also a baby fox
Kit Kat, the chocolate wafer bar

e.etymology: From Spanish Álvaro, Late Latin Alvarus, a Visigothic name. Its parts are probably Germanic all, all, or athal, noble, plus ward, guard, though other explanations exist.
A respelling of Aspen, the English name of the quaking poplar tree and of the Colorado ski town, which came into use as a given name in the US in the 1990s.

assoc.t: sounds like Aspen, the Colorado ski resort town

e.etymology: From Sanskrit arya, noble, and its Old Persian cognate; a common boys' name in India and Iran.

assoc.t: Aryan, the racial term of Nazism and white supremacists

e.note: In the US the word Aryan is strongly tied to Nazi racial ideology and white supremacist groups.
